title: Research: audience, their words, competitors, claims with sources
judge_notes: research.md is the only place the film may take a claim from. Sources are web pages the agent read; each must carry its URL and the date it was read. Facts the user gave in the brief are cited as [brief].

questions.text: Does every item under Sources have a URL and the date it was read (YYYY-MM-DD)?
Does every claim cite a listed source [S<n>] or [brief]?
Does research.md have the sections Audience, Problem, Competitors, Claims, Sources and Angle?
Does the Audience section say who buys, where they are and what they care about, specific to this brief?
Does the Problem section give the problem in the audience's own words, with a source for each phrasing?
questions.evidence: Quote one phrasing and its source id.

questions.text: Does Competitors give at least two competitors' or alternatives' angles, each with a source?
questions.evidence: Quote two angles with their source ids.

questions.text: Is every claim specific and checkable (a number, a fact, a stated quality), not vague praise?
Is every claim supported by what its cited source is summarised as saying under Sources?
questions.evidence: Quote any claim whose source does not say it.

questions.text: Are the facts the user gave in the brief (product, price, offer) in the claims list as [brief], unchanged?
questions.evidence: Quote the brief fact and the claim line.

questions.text: Is the research free of superlatives about the product or competitors (best, number one, cheapest) that no source backs?
Does the Angle section say what the video should stand on, drawn from the findings above it?
Is the research about this product, audience and market, with no generic filler that would fit any business?
